Dryads are a non-playable Fey race found in Baldur's Gate 3.

About Dryads

Dryads channel powerful druidic powers, allowing them to entangle their enemies and call forth  Wood Woads for help. They can be summoned through the spell  Conjure Woodland Being, a level four spell available to level 7 Druids.

Combat

Attacks and actions

 Entangle ()

Create a vine surface, slowing down creatures, possibly  Entangling them.

 STR Save
 Range: 18 m (60 ft)
 Fallen Lover ()

Summon a Wood Woad bound to your tree to fight alongside you.

 Range: 9 m (30 ft)
 Recharge: Short rest
 Spike Growth ( + )
Damage: 2~8
2d4⁠Piercing
Shape a piece of ground into hard spikes. A creature walking on the spikes takes 2d4⁠⁠Piercing damage for every 1.5 m (5 ft) it moves.

The spikes are Difficult Terrain, halving a creature's Movement Speed.

 Range: 18 m (60 ft)
 Strengthened Shillelagh ()

Your staff or club becomes magical: it deals 4d8Bludgeoning damage, and uses your Spellcasting Ability for Attack rolls.

 Range: Self

Dryad characters

  •  Zethino

Dryad summons

  • Dryad (Conjure Woodland Being)

Notes

  • A dryad's default attack deals 3d6+1⁠⁠Bludgeoning damage.
  • In addition to  Grasp of the Forest, both the default attack and  Strengthened Shillelagh have also another passive which can  Entangle the target. It does not have a specific name, and the save in battle log is shown as against Main Hand Attack. It uses a  DC 13 Dexterity Saving Throw.
  • If spilt, dryad blood turns into  Twisting Vines on the ground.
